capitals.name: Poma (Batán Grande)
capitals.note: 'Around 800, the Sican created the city of Poma, located at Batán Grande, in La Leche Valley'; Middle Sican centres burned and abandoned between 1050 and 1100. Coordinates approximate, not from the page and not in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Túcume
capitals.note: 'The new Late Sican capital' (undated); the Túcume page: built c. 800, 220 ha, 26 pyramids. Coordinates approximate, not from a page and not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: the Lambayeque region: the Motupe, La Leche, Lambayeque and Zaña valleys

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 750-1374: the page gives no area; it says 'The archaeological sites span the Lambayeque region, including the Motupe, La Leche, Lambayeque, and Zaña valleys'. The department of Lambayeque stands for that region.

region.text: the Lambayeque region: the Motupe, La Leche, Lambayeque and Zaña valleys

ledger.note: c. 750: the Early Sicán culture begins in Lambayeque. 'The Early Sican period began around 750 and lasted until 900'; the Sicán 'inhabited what is now the north coast of Peru between about 750 and 1375 CE'.

c. 1100: the Late Sicán capital is Túcume. The page says Túcume 'was constructed as the new Late Sican capital' after the Middle Sican centres, burned and abandoned 'between 1050 and 1100', were left; it gives no year (the Túcume page's infobox says built c. 800). Placed at the start of the Late Sicán period; page silent on the year.

region.text: the Lambayeque region: the Motupe, La Leche, Lambayeque and Zaña valleys

ledger.note: 1375: the Chimú conquer Lambayeque. 'The Late Sican period began around 1100 and ended with the conquest of the Lambayeque region by the Chimú kingdom of Chimor circa 1375'; 'By the time of the Chimú conquest of the Lambayeque region in 1375'. The Túcume page dates the Chimú occupation 1350-1450 and says nothing of a conquest in 1375.

ledger.note: 1375: the Sicán culture ends under Chimú rule.

wars.name: Chimú conquest of Lambayeque

zones.text: the Lambayeque region: the Motupe, La Leche, Lambayeque and Zaña valleys

wars.outcome: The Chimú kingdom of Chimor conquers the Lambayeque region circa 1375, ending the Late Sicán period.
wars.note: The Chimor page has the opposite wording (the 'empire of the Sican culture conquered the kingdom of Lambayeque') for an earlier time and says Pampa Grande in the Lambayeque valley 'was also ruled by the Chimú'.

sources.title: Lambayeque culture (Sicán)
sources.note: Span 750-1375, three periods, Poma at Batán Grande c. 800, Túcume as Late Sicán capital, Chimú conquest 1375.

sources.title: Túcume
sources.note: Infobox built c. 800 by the Sicán; occupations 800-1350 Lambayeque, Chimú 1350-1450, Inca 1450-1532; abandoned 1532.

notes: Wikipedia's article is 'Lambayeque culture' (also Sicán). Treated as a culture (no page calls it a state; the Chimor page speaks of a Sicán 'empire'). The Chimú conquest year is 1375 on the Lambayeque page; the Túcume page gives Chimú occupation 1350-1450 and Inca 1450-1532 (conflict with 1375 and with the Chimor page's Inca 1470). Early Sicán 750-900, Middle 900-1100, Late 1100-1375. The two capital coordinates are approximate and flagged. The Moche (north) overlap 750-800 is unresolved.
